answer: One concrete defence is SybilGuard-style admission. A new identity is accepted only if a short random walk launched from a peer-picked island of established agents reaches it fast, which is rare for clusters whose internal links vastly outnumber honest edges. A lagoon of freshly minted twins keeps bouncing back into itself, never out toward open water, so the walk times out. Honest agents sit near the horizon of that well-mixed graph, and a farm cannot buy that position: credible edges are earned over many epochs, not minted in a batch.
